$comment: What tells a person from an AI, as data, read only by run/person.cjs. JSON because no AI host's name may be a literal in code.

`aiSessionEnv`: the variables an AI host sets in every process of its session. `aiHosts`: the AI hosts, as a path part of the first two words of a process's command line; `levels`: how deep a person's terminal may sit under the root.

`askingModes`: the host's permission modes in which a hook's ask is put to a person. Whether an ask is shown under bypassPermissions is not certain (it may pass unasked), so the safe reading holds: only these.

`wrappers`: programs that can type for a person when they stand above a terminal: terminal multiplexers, tools that open a pseudo-terminal, a script runner. Lower case, by the program's name with a trailing version left off. A grave act is refused under one. A program that opens a pseudo-terminal for one command needs no name here: such a terminal holds no shell a person types into, which the walk sees by itself, and it is no person's for any verb.
`commandOption`: the option by which a shell is handed a command string instead of a person's typing.

`windows.shells`: Windows keeps no terminal sessions, so there a terminal's side ends at the farthest of these above this process (above it stand the terminal's own program and the desktop). Which words hand a Windows shell a command instead of a person's typing is the shell owner's (text/shell.json `windows`).

`hostCall.judged`: the platforms on which a hook call is told from a forged one by who holds the other end of its standard output (measured there: the host keeps it, its shell tool hands a file); on any other the call is heard as before, which is said in the trace.
